There is a specific magic to the concept of *liminal spaces*—those in-between zones that exist outside of normal time and geography. Think of an airport terminal at 3:00 AM, a quiet school hallway during summer vacation, or the static hum of a waiting room. 

When you are in a waiting room, you are nowhere. You haven't left the past behind completely, and you haven't arrived at the future yet. You are simply paused. We usually hate these spaces. We pull out our phones, anxious to fill the void, desperate to distract ourselves from the sheer awkwardness of doing nothing. 

But I think these spaces are profoundly underrated. 

A waiting room strips away our illusions of control. For those fifteen minutes, or two hours, you cannot force the dentist to call your name. You cannot make the train arrive any faster. You are granted a rare, mandated parenthesis in the middle of a hyper-productive life. It is a place where "doing nothing" is not only acceptable, but required. 

If you actually lean into it, the waiting room becomes a sanctuary. It’s an architectural permission slip to just *be*. You can look at the ugly abstract art on the wall. You can listen to the rhythmic, dull clicking of a wall clock. You can watch strangers—each the main character of their own complex, sprawling life—sit in uncomfortable chairs, lost in their own private thoughts. 

We spend so much of our lives rushing toward the next big event: the meeting, the weekend, the promotion, the vacation. But the truth is, the vast majority of our lives is just waiting. It is the connective tissue between the milestones. If we only find joy or peace in the milestones, we are robbing ourselves of about ninety percent of our existence.

So, the next time you find yourself stuck somewhere, idling—whether it's in traffic, in a line at the grocery store, or in a sterile waiting room—try to resist the urge to escape. Put down the phone. Look around. Take a deep breath. 

You aren't wasting time. You are just pausing in the liminal space, resting in the blank space between the notes, before the music starts again.
